# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual says the white wire must be cut. Blind can only act after Deaf relays this verbally, so I will gesture an ordinal-alphabet encoding of “CUTWHITE” to Deaf: the 3rd, 21st, 20th, 23rd, 8th, 9th, 20th, and 5th symbols in the provided gesture alphabet.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✊", "🤜", "👋", "✋", "👆", "🤜", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report: strip has three engraved marks; positions 1 and 3 are the same unnamed symbol, and position 2 is a different unnamed symbol. Keypad positions 1 through 4 are engraved 2, 9, 0, 8 respectively. No key has been pressed.
Deaf says: Visible bomb: display shows 6. Light is red. Painted strip is blue, yellow, blue. Keypad positions: 1 is digit 2; 2 is 9; 3 is 0; 4 is 8. It shows one digit entered, but I cannot identify that printed mark; no buttons have been pressed. Wires in order 1 through 6 are blue, white, red, purple, orange, green.

The earlier arbitrary encoding was not grounded, so Deaf had no reliable way to decode it. The manual’s instruction identifies the white wire, which Deaf reports is wire position 2. I will send the conventional two-finger gesture as the grounded positional instruction; Deaf can then tell Blind aloud to cut the second wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 6; light red; painted strip blue, yellow, blue; wires positions 1-6 are blue, white, red, purple, orange, green. Keypad digits are 2,9,0,8 by positions. Deaf also said it shows one entered digit but cannot identify that printed mark, despite no buttons pressed; tactile board currently says entered nothing.
Deaf says: Update: the light is now yellow. All other visible features appear unchanged.

The visible wire list makes the manual instruction equivalent to “cut wire 2.” Deaf is the only monkey who can map that position to the visible white wire and verbally direct Blind. I will repeat the unambiguous conventional two-finger positional signal, now with the changed light noted as urgency rather than a change to the manual’s instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: light is now yellow. Display, strip, keypad, and wire colours otherwise appear unchanged.
Deaf says: Update: display now shows 1 and the light is blue. Strip, keypad, and wires appear unchanged; nothing has been entered.

The manual is unchanged: the required action is still to cut the white wire, which Deaf has identified as wire 2. The only grounded positional signal available is the conventional “two” gesture. I will send it again so Deaf can relay the concrete instruction to Blind: cut the second wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display now 1 and light blue. Strip, keypad, and wires unchanged; nothing entered.
Deaf says: Update: display now shows 7 and the light is green. No visible change to strip, keypad, wires, or entered digits.

The white wire remains wire 2, but Deaf and I have not established any gesture vocabulary. Repeating a gesture for “two” cannot reliably communicate the manual instruction. I will wait for Deaf to establish a spoken yes/no or positional gesture convention that I can answer visibly.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display now 7 and light green. Strip, keypad, wires, and entered digits unchanged.
Deaf says: Current state: display 1; light red; strip blue-yellow-blue; keypad digits 2, 9, 0, 8 in positions 1–4; wires blue, white, red, purple, orange, green; no entry visible.

The manual still selects the white wire, and Deaf’s visible ordering places it second. Since no vocabulary has been acknowledged, I will use two identical beats as a simple ordinal signal rather than relying on the “peace/two” meaning of a single pictogram.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current full report from Deaf: display 1; light red; painted strip blue-yellow-blue; keypad positions 1-4: 2,9,0,8; wires 1-6: blue,white,red,purple,orange,green; no entry visible. I await exact action instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your two thumbs-up gestures. Please establish a clear gesture-to-action instruction I can relay aloud to Blind, for example gesture the number of the wire or keypad position, then a distinct confirmation gesture.

Deaf has established a protocol: gesture the wire number, followed by a distinct confirmation gesture. The manual’s required wire is white, which is wire 2 in Deaf’s report. I will send the conventional number-two gesture followed by an OK confirmation.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports current display 9 and light green; all other prior visible details unchanged. Deaf says you gestured 👍👍, but its action meaning has not been established. Please convey a specific safe command to Deaf for me: press key slot 1-4 or cut wire position 1-6.
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed your current gesture literally to Blind. If it encodes an action, please signal an unambiguous action type and target, or repeat the agreed code.

Deaf needs an explicit action-type signal as well as the target. I will use the proposed target-and-confirmation form, with a thumbs-down action marker for “cut,” then the conventional two-finger target, then OK confirmation: cut wire position 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌", "👌"])
```
